cards.title: Uniform convergence under Dobrushin dependence
cards.formal: For every a∈[0,1), does there exist a finite constant C_a such that the following holds uniformly? Let m≥1, let H be a nonempty class of measurable binary functions on a measurable instance space X with finite VC dimension d, and let P_m be a joint law of S=(Z₁,…,Z_m), Z_i=(X_i,Y_i)∈X×{0,1}, whose marginals all equal D and whose total-variation Dobrushin coefficient is at most a. For every δ∈(0,1), require Pr_{S∼P_m}[sup_{h∈H}|L_S(h)−L_D(h)|>C_a√((d+log(2/δ))/m)]≤δ. Here L_S and L_D are zero-one losses and the conditional-kernel and measurability conventions below are part of the model. This card reads the source’s proposed extension quantitatively, using the iid-order finite-VC rate stated in equation (18) of its full version; it is not merely a claim that some unspecified convergence rate exists.
cards.why: Would determine whether the standard weak-influence condition suffices for the uniform statistical guarantees that make finite VC dimension useful, beyond the already-known existence of a successful learner.
cards.status_note: Read the source definitions, its learning theorem and the stronger uniform-convergence theorem in the conference and full versions. Searches through 12 September 2026 did not locate a proof or refutation of the displayed ordinary-Dobrushin finite-VC rate. The 2026 product-space uniform-law paper concerns another estimator and distributional structure, not this empirical-mean extension. The lack of a located resolution is not an exhaustive current-status guarantee.

cards.definitions: Write Z=X×{0,1}. For each i, take a probability kernel κ_i(·|z_{−i}) that is a version of the conditional law of Z_i given all other coordinates under P_m. These kernels are defined on the entire product Z^{m−1}, including configurations of zero marginal probability. For i≠j define c_{ij}=sup{TV(κ_i(·|u),κ_i(·|v)):u,v∈Z^{m−1}, u and v agree except possibly in coordinate j}, where TV(μ,ν)=sup_{B measurable}|μ(B)−ν(B)|. In a finite space this is one half of the sum of absolute probability differences. The admissibility promise is existence of such conditional-kernel versions with max_i Σ_{j≠i}c_{ij}≤a. Thus the influence of coordinate j on coordinate i is bounded, and the sum is over influences entering i; it is not a column-sum or a Markov-chain mixing-time condition. Specifying versions on null configurations prevents undefined conditioning from deciding the promise. Kernels satisfying this global bound and a measurable random supremum in the displayed event are assumed; these are the explicit regularity conventions for the source’s conditional-distribution notation. No independence, graph degree, spatial dimension, stationarity or exchangeability beyond identical marginals is assumed. For h:X→{0,1}, L_S(h)=m⁻¹Σ_i 1{h(X_i)≠Y_i}, and L_D(h)=E_{(X,Y)∼D}1{h(X)≠Y}. A finite F⊆X is shattered if every binary labeling of F is the restriction of a member of H. VC(H) is the largest size of a shattered set, or infinity if these sizes are unbounded. The hypothesis d<∞ includes d=0. The constant C_a may depend on the fixed upper bound a and may diverge as a approaches one, but must be independent of m,d,δ,X,H,D and P_m. The law P_m may be different for each m; no consistency of an infinite process is required. The logarithm is natural. This is a statistical inequality, with no algorithmic running-time requirement.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove existence of such a constant for every fixed a<1, uniformly over all the displayed models and parameters, or refute this quantified rate. A negative answer must defeat every proposed constant for some fixed a<1; a family with its coefficient tending to one does not by itself suffice. Proving generalization only for a particular learner, a bound depending on the cardinality of H, a slower rate, or a result needing stronger log-influence assumptions does not establish the displayed extension.

cards.title: Untuned switching regret for oblivious adversarial bandits
cards.formal: Does there exist a randomized bandit algorithm A and universal constants C>0 and p≥0 such that the following holds? For every number of arms K≥2, horizon T≥1 and loss sequence ℓ₁,…,ℓ_T∈[0,1]ᴷ fixed before play, give A only K and T. Simultaneously for every integer S∈{0,…,T−1}, require R_S(A;ℓ)≤C√(K(S+1)T)[log(2KT)]ᵖ, where R_S is the expected loss of A minus the loss of the best hindsight arm sequence with at most S switches. The same algorithm, without S or a bound on S as input, must satisfy every one of these inequalities. This is the remaining oblivious-adversary case of the source question; the corresponding general adaptive-adversary target was subsequently ruled out.
cards.why: Would determine whether finite-arm exploration can adapt to every comparator’s rate of change without prior tuning, unifying optimal static and tracking guarantees for arbitrary fixed loss sequences.
cards.status_note: Read the source question and later papers distinguishing stochastic distribution changes, pointwise best-arm switches and hindsight comparator switches. The February 2026 preprint explicitly retains the general untuned benchmark question. Also checked the March 2026 unconstrained linear-bandit preprint, whose action space differs. No resolution of the stated oblivious finite-arm target was found through 12 September 2026; this is not an exhaustive search or independent proof audit.

cards.definitions: At round t, A chooses an arm I_t∈[K]={1,…,K} using K, T, its random bits and the previously chosen arms and observed losses. It incurs and observes only the scalar ℓ_t(I_t). It does not see the other coordinates of ℓ_t or receive any announcement when losses or comparator arms change. The entire sequence of loss vectors is chosen independently of the learner’s realized random bits before the first round; arbitrary variation from round to round is allowed. For an arm sequence j=(j₁,…,j_T)∈[K]ᵀ put s(j)=|{t∈{2,…,T}:j_t≠j_{t−1}}|. Define R_S(A;ℓ)=E_A[Σ_{t=1}^T ℓ_t(I_t)]−min_{j:s(j)≤S}Σ_{t=1}^Tℓ_t(j_t). The expectation is only over A’s randomness. Comparators may be chosen with full knowledge of the loss sequence and are not required to select a pointwise best arm. S counts switches, so S+1 counts the maximum number of constant-arm segments and S=0 recovers static regret. The logarithm is natural; C and p are independent of K,T,S and ℓ. This specifies the meaning of the target bound up to logarithmic factors. Since R_S≤T automatically, the bound is informative only where its right side is smaller than T. Simultaneous means all these expected-regret guarantees hold for one A; it does not demand a simultaneous high-probability event. The question imposes no separate running-time or memory bound. An adaptive adversary, which may set future loss vectors in response to realized past actions, is a different model excluded from this remaining question.
cards.answer_criterion: Give one algorithm with a proof of the displayed uniform expected-regret bounds for all finite K,T, fixed loss sequences and switch budgets, or prove that no such algorithm and universal constants exist. Tuning the algorithm to S, bounding only regret to the pointwise best arm by its number of changes, or establishing a lower bound that needs an adaptive adversary is insufficient for this oblivious switching-comparator question.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
